title: Session-aware minimums with graceful decay — proposal & pilot
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Background: Enterprise customers frequently run long-lived interactive sessions (chat assistants, agent loops) where token shape is highly front-loaded. Current per-token minimums and simple session floors cause sharp jumps in billed spend or force customers to overcommit reserved capacity. Proposal: introduce a session-aware minimum that applies a time-decaying floor to a session's billable tokens plus an optional grace credit buffer for the first N minutes. The mechanism aims to smooth charges across short bursts and prolonged sessions while preserving incentives to optimize token efficiency.
rationale: We want a pricing primitive that: (1) reduces friction for conversational product teams that are sensitive to mid-session token bursts, (2) avoids creating incentives for artificially long sessions to amortize cost, and (3) is simple enough for sales/legal to include in enterprise contracts. Graceful decay means the floor reduces at a defined rate (e.g., 20% per 10 minutes) until it reaches zero or a small residual per-session minimum. This balances revenue predictability with customer fairness.
metrics: Primary metrics: effective $/token for pilot customers, % of sessions billed by floor vs actual tokens, churn risk signals from pilot cohort, incremental ARR from converted pilots. Targets for pilot: reduce billing surprises (CS escalations) by 60% for trial cohort; <5% negative margin delta vs baseline; no measurable increase in abusive long-session behavior after 30d.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDK/server-side gating implemented and feature-flagged in hosted API; 2) Billing pipeline shows per-session floor applied and decayed in telemetry; 3) Pilot launched with 3 enterprise customers and billing reports accessible to Billing/Sales; 4) Legal sign-off on draft contract text and security questionnaire addendum; 5) No stability regressions in runtime (latency or throughput) attributable to floor computation.
implementation_notes: - Add session_id-aware metering layer in hosted ingestion path. - Compute a rolling 'floor allowance' per session that decays on wall-clock or active-token time (configurable). - Support both symmetric and asymmetric IO weighting (configurable per-customer). - Expose per-session floor and remaining grace credit via Console telemetry and per-invoice line items. - Feature-flag rollout: admin-only -> beta opt-in -> GA. - Requires small schema update to billing events and export format.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (spec & legal): finalize contract language and SQ addendum (2 weeks). Phase 1 (engineering): implement feature-flagged meter & telemetry (4 weeks). Phase 2 (pilot): 3 enterprise pilots for 6 weeks with Sales/CS handoff; weekly checkpoints. Phase 3 (analysis): evaluate metrics, iterate decay curve and defaults (2 weeks). Phase 4 (GA): marketing + SDK updates + docs + Pricing page update.
risks: - Complexity in billing pipeline increases invoice review time; mitigated by line-item transparency. - Customers may game decay parameters to keep long sessions artificially alive; mitigate via active-token decay fallback and fraud detection heuristics. - Legal/SQ may require explicit language for how logs and telemetry are stored for audited billing; engage Security early.
dependencies_details: Depends on ENG work to emit session_id in billing events (ENG-21845) and a billing export schema update (PM-712000). Sales/Legal must agree on contract wording and grace credit definitions. Console team needs a dashboard tile for per-session floor visualization.

notes_for_sales_and_legal: Suggested contract language (summary): 'Customer will be billed based on actual billable tokens. For interactive sessions, a configurable session floor with a defined decay schedule may apply. Any grace credits are applied at invoice reconciliation and clearly itemized. Redwood will provide per-session telemetry for audit; retention and redaction practices follow our standard billing telemetry policy (see SQ addendum). Sales: include a pilot appendix with selected decay params and opt-out clause.'
post_mortem_checklist: If pilot shows >5% negative margin impact: revert to conservative decay defaults, pause new pilots, and run targeted price elasticity tests. If customers report invoice confusion: add per-session statement on invoice and expand CS playbook.
security_notes: Security asked for explicit statement of telemetry retention window (suggested 120 days) and a KMS/HSM reference for any exported billing archives. Will include SQ addendum in pilot contracts.
